digest.definition: A science-based degree with a strong vocational focus, meant to make graduates ready to register as veterinary nurses when they graduate
distinctiveFeatures: A science-based degree with a strong vocational focus, meant to make graduates ready to register as veterinary nurses when they graduate
Veterinary nurses give professional care grounded in knowledge of each patient's condition, across many settings and every life stage, mindful of the owner or keeper
The work aims at animal health, welfare and quality of life with as little pain and suffering as possible, and can be proactive or reactive, autonomous or collaborative
Registered nurses may give medical treatment and minor surgery that does not enter a body cavity, under a veterinary surgeon's direction, and educate owners and the public
Practice is regulated through RCVS registration, a code of conduct with five principles, continuing development and fitness to practise
Licence to practise courses are built around the RCVS Day One Competences, Skills and Professional Behaviours and long clinical placements in approved training practices
Courses cover a range of species, with small animal and equine routes and, in some places, farm animal husbandry
The statement covers three awards side by side: foundation degree, honours degree and master's degree

subjectSpecific.text: You should become able to handle situations that need an ethical stance, seeing the risks and using the relevant law when you need to.
You should become able to speak up for patients and clients while always keeping their information confidential.

transferable.text: You should become able to work in a team of different professionals, communicate very well and keep professional relationships with clients, colleagues and the public, even when things are emotionally or financially tense.
You should become able to base your decisions on research and up-to-date data and take responsibility for what you do.
You should become able to keep reflecting on your own practice to see what to improve next.

statements.appliesTo: veterinary nurses who wish to practise in the UK
statements.about: registration, the code of conduct and accountability
statements.paraphrase: Anyone who wants to practise as a veterinary nurse in the UK must be on the RCVS register and must commit to its code of conduct, answering for their actions and keeping their knowledge current through reflective continuing professional development; fitness to practise procedures hold them to account.

forPractitioner.text: Practice in the UK must rest on RCVS registration, a commitment to its code, accountability and regular reflective CPD; the course is where students first meet these professional obligations.

forBeneficiary.text: To work as a veterinary nurse in the UK you must join the RCVS register, keep to its code of conduct, answer for what you do and keep your skills current through professional development that you reflect on.

statements.about: courses that prepare graduates for registration on graduating
statements.paraphrase: The statement sets out the nature and academic standards of veterinary nursing degrees: a science-based, strongly vocational course that should prepare graduates to register as veterinary nurses on graduating.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course as science-based and strongly vocational so that it should leave graduates ready to register as veterinary nurses on the day they graduate.

statements.about: the Day One Competences, Skills and Professional Behaviours
statements.paraphrase: An RCVS-accredited licence to practise course should be built so that graduates can gain and show the Day One Competences, the Day One Skills List and the Professional Behaviours and Attributes, the RCVS minimum that every student veterinary nurse must meet to join its register.

forPractitioner.text: Build an accredited licence to practise course so that students should be able to gain and evidence the Day One Competences, Skills and Professional Behaviours; the RCVS sets these as the minimum for joining its register.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should be set up so that you can gain and show the Day One Competences, the Day One Skills and the professional behaviours; the RCVS requires you to meet them before you can join its register.

statements.about: personal responsibility for equity and inclusive practice

forPractitioner.text: Design the programme so that it should foster openness and each student's responsibility for equity and inclusion, framed as a professional duty in teamwork and in educating owners and the public.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you see equity and inclusion as part of your own professional responsibility, in your team and when you advise animal owners and the public.
